# Story Pts / Cmts Why it's worth reading
1 Local Wikipedia: Wikipedia, but only for things a half hour walk from you 322 / 83 Front end over geocoded Wikipedia articles showing the 25 closest places (or up to 500 within ~6 miles), with the lookup done in-browser so shared links never carry your location1
2 Docker is weird 449 / 212 Notes from writing a toy container runtime: containers are plain kernel processes plus namespaces/cgroups, images are folders reached via pivot_root, and runc needs a C nsenter shim because Go is multi-threaded and has no real fork2
3 How does Fable 5.1 hide messages in images? 77 / 19 Over 50 messages, Fable 5.1 invented its own shape-height and object-tilt encodings inside SVGs; a fresh instance decoded 78% from screenshots alone, while GPT-6 Astra preferred Morse code and acrostics (cross-model: 44/50 and 42/50)3
4 The alien space of science 47 / 3 NeurIPS 2026 paper clusters 16,068 LLM papers into "idea atoms" and ranks coherent-but-unlikely combinations, recovering 2025 research directions from under 1% of candidates at 35.9× chance4
5 The foolishness of "natural language programming" (1978) 154 / 96 Dijkstra: pushing work across an interface costs more than it saves, and the "naturalness" of our native tongue is just the ease of uttering nonsense that isn't obviously nonsense5
6 The HTML-in-Canvas API origin trial 38 / 16 HTML inside a canvas is now drawn into 2D/WebGL/WebGPU while staying selectable, accessible, translatable and find-in-page-able — dissolving the old DOM-vs-canvas tradeoff6
7 OpenShell – safe runtime for fleets of autonomous AI agents 389 / 191 NVIDIA sandboxes each agent with kernel-level file/syscall/network policy, injects credentials only for approved endpoints, and formally verifies every policy change before applying it7
